cosy-lesson.title: "We should turn off AI for a week to see if people's brains still work.": Anonymous

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Artificial – made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally.

p.em: Example: Relying on artificial intelligence might weaken our natural critical thinking.

cosy-blockquote.p: Automation – the use of automatic equipment or systems to do work.

p.em: Example: The complete automation of writing could make students forget how to compose essays.

cosy-blockquote.p: Reliance – dependency on or trust in someone or something.

p.em: Example: Our heavy reliance on digital navigators has ruined our ability to read physical maps.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cognitive – relating to the mental processes of perception, memory, and judgment.

p.em: Example: Outsourcing simple calculations to apps can affect our cognitive abilities.

cosy-blockquote.p: Brain – the organ of the body in the head that controls thought and feeling.

p.em: Example: The brain is like a muscle that needs regular exercise to stay strong and healthy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Detachment – the state of being objective, distant, or disconnected.

p.em: Example: Taking a week of digital detachment helps us regain mental clarity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Habits – settled or regular tendencies or practices that are hard to give up.

p.em: Example: Checking our phones immediately upon waking is one of the most common habits.

cosy-blockquote.p: Algorithm – a process or set of rules followed by a computer in calculations.

p.em: Example: The search engine algorithm decides what information we see first.

cosy-blockquote.p: Outsourcing – the practice of obtaining services or solving tasks from an external source.

p.em: Example: The outsourcing of simple decisions to software makes life effortless but passive.

cosy-blockquote.p: Process – a series of actions or steps taken in order to achieve a particular end.

p.em: Example: Learning is a slow process that cannot be bypassed by automated summaries.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
What are the risks of using artificial assistance for creative writing or drawing?
★ How often do you use artificial intelligence in your daily work or study?

Will the complete automation of daily tasks make humans more creative or more passive?
★ Which automated task are you most grateful for in your life?

How does our constant reliance on smartphones affect our long-term memory?
★ Can you navigate your city without using a digital map?

In what ways does typing instead of writing by hand affect our cognitive development?
★ Do you find it easier to remember things when you write them down on paper?

Do you agree that the human brain is slowly losing its ability to concentrate?
★ What do you do to keep your brain active and sharp?

What benefits can a person experience from a week of complete digital detachment?
★ Have you ever tried a digital detox weekend?

How can we build healthy digital habits in a world designed to keep us distracted?
★ What is one bad digital habit you would like to break?

To what extent do you feel your personal interests are controlled by a social media algorithm?
★ Have you ever bought something just because an algorithm recommended it?

Is outsourcing our thinking processes to technology a real threat to human intelligence?
★ What mental task do you happily outsource to computers?

Why is the slow process of struggling with a problem vital for genuine learning?
★ Tell us about a complex process you recently had to learn.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In a future world fully governed by artificial agents, human intuition will be completely ignored. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you adapt if artificial systems became entirely obsolete in tomorrow's world?

The rapid speed of modern society will eventually make manual labor and the refusal of automation highly respected practices. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you use technology to artificially automate your personal creative hobbies?

Future schools will prioritize personal independence over digital reliance. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you want future generations of your family to remember your relationship with digital reliance?

As artificial intelligence advances, machines will exhibit a superior capacity for cognitive analysis compared to humans. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could design a futuristic school, how would you teach cognitive skills to children?

In the coming decades, direct neural links to the brain will become a highly commercialized luxury commodity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where brain activity is fully managed or monitored by digital algorithms?

The survival of human civilization will depend on our collective ability to practice digital detachment. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you personally prepare for a future where detachment is increasingly rare?

Future generations will look back at our current online habits with deep skepticism. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send a single message about habits to people living 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make escaping any corporate algorithm incredibly difficult to maintain. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic utopia that completely guarantees comfort at the cost of your freedom?

In the future, social status will be determined by a person's refusal of digital outsourcing rather than wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope outsourcing will play in your own personal future over the next decade?

A future world governed entirely by logic will have no space left for the slow mystery of the creative process. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If a machine could perfectly replicate your creative process, would you still value it?

ul.li: Incorrect: He have went to Paris → Correct: He has gone to Paris ((Present perfect third-person singular 'has' + past participle 'gone'.))

Incorrect: We discussed about the problem → Correct: We discussed the problem / had a discussion about the problem (('Discuss' is transitive and takes no preposition, or use 'have a discussion about'.))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Use 'agree' directly as a verb rather than using it with the auxiliary 'am'.))
